source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Discuss the issue only with coworkers because negotiated grievance procedures should not be used","B":"Assume every workplace uses identical grievance rules regardless of the applicable labor agreement","C":"Use the negotiated grievance or appeal process and follow the agreement's documented steps and timelines","D":"Resign immediately because a covered disciplinary decision cannot be reviewed through a grievance process"}}
source_row.rationale: When a collective-bargaining agreement provides a grievance procedure for a disciplinary dispute, the employee should use the negotiated process and its required steps, representation rights, and timelines. Procedures vary by agreement and law.
source_row.source_detail: NLRA Sections 9(a) and 203(d): employee grievances and agreed grievance-dispute resolution under collective-bargaining agreements; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: National Labor Relations Board — National Labor Relations Act
source_row.stem: A union-represented nurse wants to challenge a disciplinary action covered by the collective-bargaining agreement. Which approach is most appropriate?
